UDc 621-883 14 IS : 7381 " 1986 



Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2003 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

HAND OPERATED SQUARE DRIVE 

SOCKET WRENCHES 

( First Revision ) 



1. Scope — Covers the dimensions and other requirements for hand operated square drive socket 
wrenches used m conjunction with tommy bars, cranks, ratchets or any other connecting part having 
square driving ends conforming to IS : 7214-1974 'Driving squares for hand socket wrenches'. 

2. Dimensions -— Dimensions shall be as given in Table 1 . 

2.1 Tolerances on Width Across Flats — As specified for forged and subsequently unmachined 
spanners in IS : 2027-1980 'Width across flats for spanners and sockets (second revision)'. 

3. Material — Suitable steels meeting the requirements laid down in 5. 

Example: 

Steel designation, T50 Cr4 V2 of 13:3749-1978 'Tool and die steel for cold working 
( first revision )'. 

4. Designation — Hand operated square drive socket wrench of nominal size 30, that is, width 
across flats 30 mm and using 20 mm drive square on other end and having single hexagon operating 
end shall be designated as: 

Socket Wrench 30 x 20S IS : 7381 . 
Note — For double hexagon the symbol 'D' shall be used. 

5. Hardness, Workmanship and Finish, Torque Testing and Sampling — Shall be in accordance 
with IS: 6131-1980 'Technical requirements for hand operated wrenches ( spanners ) and sockets 
{first revision)'. The torque values shall conform to series 'E' of IS : 6131-1980. 

6. Marking — Each socket wrench shall be marked with its nominal size, that is, width across flats 
and the size of the driving square near its respective ends and manufacturers name, initials or 
recognized trade-mark. 

6.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



EXP LAN ATOR Y NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1974. The present revision has been taken up in order to 
include the wrenches of nominal sizes 35, 4'5, 6, 9, 15, 16, 18, 21, 34, 65, 70, 75 and 80 mm since 
these sizes are also popularly being used. While revising, long execution and short execution 
wrenches have also been included. Short execution sizes are standardized whereas the long executions 
are recommendatory. Long execution sizes are also used as spark plug wrenches. 

This revised standard is in alignment with DIN 3124-1980 'Square drive socket wrenches for 
hexagon bolts, hand operated', issued by Deutsches Institut fur Normung (DIN) which is further in 
alignment with ISO/DIS 2725-1985 'Assembly tools for screws and nuts— Power and hand operated 
square drive sockets— Metric and inch series', issued by International Organization for Standardization 
(ISO).
